Sir:-

Reference attached letter.

I with C.D.I. Wei made inquiries at each of the
following shops on Wuchow Road (as letter signed
"from Merchants doing business on Wuchow Rd.,)
on 14-5-30 if any of them had written, or knew anything
of a letter written to the Police, concerning a
member thereof. Each of them stated they had not written
nor did they know of any letter so written.

C.D.C. I64 states he had a reception and feast in his
home (628 Wuchow Road) on II-5-30. This was on the
occasion of his adopted son's wedding and there were
only 90 invitations (The adopted son is the legal son
of the C.D.C's nephew; adopted in accordance with
Chinese custom the C.D.C. not having a son of his own)
The C.D.C. had asked me previous to holding this reception
if it was permissible for him to do so, it not being
on an elaborate scale. I told him yes, but for him to
also inform the D.D.D.
The C.D.C. denies that he has the bad characters mentioned
as his followers.
I have always found this C.D.C. a good man, and active
from time to time in rounding up criminal gangs.

Translation of a letter addressed to Mr. Aiers,
Police Headquarters, purporting to have
been sent by one 沈 Sing on Wuchow Rd.

sir,

I beg to bring to your notice that
C.D.C. Zee Vung Tsong (徐文忠) attached to the
Hongkew Police Station has been in the practice of
recruiting followers, who are either Cantonese brothel
keepers on Miller, Woosung and Derpoe Roads, or second
hand goods dealers on Wuchow Road, or robbers and loafers.

Zee Vung Tsong will celebrate the birthday
anniversary of his mother between 5 and 8 p.m. on May 11
(? the 11th. day of the 5th. moon). He has distributed
more than 2,000 invitation cards, thereby spoiling the
reputation of the Police Force of the S.M.C. The
celebration and the feast will take place at his home,
No. 608 Kiang Auh Lee (江夏里) alleyway on Wuchow Road.

Should you be in doubt regarding my report
you may detail men to institute an investigation. Those
attending the feast will be brothel-keepers, stolen goods
receivers, loafers and notorious robbers exclusively.

May 11, 1930
